correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge3\), the smooth codimension-six zero locus in \(\operatorname{Gr}(3,2n+1)\) has Chow class \(c_3(\bigwedge^2S^\vee)^2\). The verified five-term Schur expansion, Pieri rule and three-row hook formula give the exact top Plucker-degree ratio 8(8R^3-24R^2+10R+15)/(R(R+1)(R+2)), R=2n-2. The exact factorizations ratio-1=3(R-2)(3R-5)(7R+4)/den and 64-ratio=24(2R-1)(8R+5)/den are positive for R>=4. Since \(d=6(n-2)\ge6\) and \(H^2\cong\mathbb Z\), an integral graded ring isomorphism would force the ratio to be an integer dth power, impossible between \(1\) and \(2^d\). This uses only additive rank from the source; no unproved hyperplane primitivity is needed. Cellular cycle maps establish the integral Chow-ring analogue. The standalone verify.py checks the Schur identity and global algebraic identities by exact polynomial arithmetic, plus independent finite numeric instances.

value.rationale: Fonarev--Kuznetsov expressly identify the unexplored multiplicative structure as important. A rank-three infinite-family nonisomorphism answers that natural comparison for the first higher-rank locus, not one cherry-picked degree; the strict full-range obstruction follows from a new exact codimension-six Schubert computation. The top-degree ratio approaches 64 while graded Betti numbers agree, revealing a quantitative structural failure of additive rigidity. This is more than a low-effort type check, generic textbook corollary, or arbitrary finite slice; no full ring presentation is claimed.
